name: Bridgewater Legal Group PLLC
description: A 12-person law firm in downtown Grand Rapids specializing in real estate transactions, small business law, and estate planning. Founded in 2015 by partners Aisha Patel and David Kowalski, who left a larger firm to serve small businesses and families in the GR community. Revenue of approximately $1.9M annually. Well-regarded locally but struggling to scale because internal operations haven't kept pace with client growth.

team.name: Aisha Patel
team.responsibilities: Real estate and business law. Firm strategy. Reviews all significant documents. Perpetually overbooked.

team.name: David Kowalski
team.responsibilities: Estate planning and probate. Manages his own caseload. Less involved in day-to-day operations.

team.name: Rachel Torres
team.responsibilities: 2 years at the firm. Handles real estate closings and contract reviews. Spends hours drafting documents that follow the same patterns.

team.name: Marcus Webb
team.responsibilities: 1 year at the firm. Estate planning and small business formation. Drafts many first versions of documents.

team.name: Kim Nguyen
team.responsibilities: 15 years experience. Manages case files, prepares document drafts, coordinates with title companies and courts. The operational backbone of the firm.

team.name: Jason Li
team.responsibilities: 3 years experience. Supports Marcus and David. Handles intake paperwork and initial document preparation.

team.name: Olivia Grant
team.responsibilities: Front desk, phones, scheduling, mail. Manages the new client intake process. First impression for every client.

team.name: Tom Brennan
team.responsibilities: Billing via Clio, accounts receivable, vendor management, IT liaison. Wears many hats.

team.name: Legal Interns
team.responsibilities: Law students from Cooley Law School. Research and basic document prep.

toolStack.name: Clio (Law Practice Management)
toolStack.usage: Case management, time tracking, billing. They use approximately 40% of its capabilities. Intake forms are basic.
painPoints: Only 40% of features are actively used
Intake forms haven't been updated in 2+ years
No automation of routine tasks despite Clio supporting it
Time tracking is inconsistent — attorneys forget to log

toolStack.name: Microsoft 365
toolStack.usage: Word for all document drafting. Outlook for email. SharePoint for file storage — poorly organized with no consistent naming conventions.
painPoints: SharePoint is poorly organized — files are hard to find
No document templates library — attorneys copy old documents
Find-and-replace errors (wrong client name left in) have reached clients
No version control on draft documents

toolStack.name: DocuSign
toolStack.usage: E-signatures for closings and contracts. Works well in isolation but is not connected to Clio or document storage.
painPoints: Disconnected from Clio — signed docs must be manually uploaded
No automated reminders to signers
Completed envelopes require manual filing in SharePoint

toolStack.name: Zoom
toolStack.usage: Client meetings — about 30% are now virtual. No transcription or automated follow-up.
painPoints: No meeting transcription or AI notes
Action items are captured informally or not at all
No automated follow-up email after client consultations

toolStack.name: Paper Intake Forms
toolStack.usage: New clients fill out a paper form at the front desk. Olivia then types the information into Clio and Word templates.
painPoints: Double data entry — paper to Clio to Word
Slow intake process loses potential clients
No digital intake option for remote or after-hours inquiries

toolStack.name: Excel
toolStack.usage: Tracks accounts receivable, firm financials, and marketing spend. Manual data entry from Clio exports.
painPoints: Manual export from Clio creates data lag
No real-time financial visibility
Prone to formula errors

toolStack.name: Google Business Profile
toolStack.usage: Occasionally responds to reviews. No systematic review generation strategy.
painPoints: No system for soliciting reviews from satisfied clients
Negative reviews sometimes go unanswered for days
No tracking of review volume vs. competitors

workflows.name: New Client Intake
workflows.description: The process from a prospective client's first contact to an active, properly set-up case in Clio.
workflows.currentProcess: Potential client calls or emails → Olivia captures basic info on paper form → sends info to the relevant attorney via email → attorney decides whether to take the case (sometimes 2-3 days later) → if yes, Olivia types info into Clio and sends an engagement letter template → client comes in to sign and provide documents → Jason or Kim creates the case file.
painPoints: 7-10 days from first contact to active case
Slow response time loses prospective clients to competing firms
Paper-to-digital double entry wastes Olivia's time
No tracking of leads who don't convert
Attorneys can't quickly assess case viability before investing time
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could pre-screen inquiries for conflicts of interest, classify the matter type and urgency, draft a personalized acknowledgment email, create the case file in Clio, and notify the appropriate attorney with a structured summary — reducing intake time from days to hours.

workflows.name: Document Drafting
workflows.description: The process of creating legal documents — purchase agreements, LLC articles, wills, leases — for client matters.
workflows.currentProcess: Attorney or paralegal opens a previous similar document in Word → saves a new copy → manually finds and replaces client names, dates, property addresses, and other case-specific details → reviews for accuracy → sends to senior attorney for review.
painPoints: Find-and-replace errors (wrong client names) have reached clients — embarrassing and potentially problematic
1-3 hours per document for routine drafts that follow standard patterns
Rachel and Marcus spend 60%+ of their time on drafting instead of higher-value work
No document template library — every attorney has their own approach
No version tracking on draft documents
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could generate first drafts of routine documents from structured intake data, dramatically reducing drafting time and eliminating find-and-replace errors. Attorneys shift from drafters to reviewers.

workflows.name: Client Communication & Status Updates
workflows.description: Keeping clients informed about the status of their matter throughout the engagement.
workflows.currentProcess: Clients email or call for status updates → Olivia takes a message or forwards the email → attorney responds when they get to it (sometimes days later) → no proactive updates go out.
painPoints: Clients frequently feel left in the dark
Olivia fields 15-20 'where is my case?' calls per week — pure admin overhead
Attorneys spend significant time on status emails that could be standardized
No proactive notification system for milestones or next steps
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could send proactive status update emails when case milestones are hit (document sent, signature received, closing scheduled), reducing inbound status calls by an estimated 60-70%.

workflows.name: Billing & Collections
workflows.description: Monthly invoice generation, delivery, tracking, and collection follow-up.
workflows.currentProcess: Attorneys log time in Clio (inconsistently). Tom generates invoices monthly → reviews with attorneys who add forgotten entries → sends invoices → manually tracks payments → sends overdue reminders via email.
painPoints: Significant unbilled time — attorneys forget to log hours
Overdue accounts represent ~$180K at any given time
52-day average collection time (industry benchmark is 30-35 days)
Tom spends 2 full days per month on collections follow-up
No automated payment reminder sequence
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could run an automated collections sequence (email reminders at 15, 30, 45 days), flag unbilled time for attorney review, and generate a weekly collections dashboard for Tom.
